headline: Booking.com launches Lola, an AI travel agent
summary: Lola offers personalized recommendations, live availability, and direct booking, with subscription tiers for added benefits.
details: Booking.com has unveiled Lola, a new AI assistant designed to act as a personal travel agent. Lola promises to provide personalized recommendations, real-time availability and pricing, direct booking capabilities, preferred rates, and exclusive benefits.

The AI assistant can recommend and reserve hotels, restaurants, events, activities, or even entire trips. Booking.com has partnered with several companies including ResX, CLEAR, BLADE, Aero, SeatGeek, GetYourGuide, Nuitee, and Ten Group, alongside its own brands like KAYAK and Agoda.

Lola understands natural language, asks follow-up questions, and learns user preferences to tailor recommendations. It allows users to compare options and make bookings within the same conversational interface, searching real-time availability and pricing.

While Lola is free to use, certain premium services require a subscription. The 'Plus' tier costs $5 per month and the 'VIP' tier is $25 per month, both with a 12-month commitment. These tiers offer benefits such as discounts on hotels, priority event access, and premium airport services.

Lola enters a growing market of AI travel agents, with Meta's Muse offering similar functionalities. However, the article notes the potential for AI agents to "hallucinate" or make errors, citing an example where an AI booked a hotel in the wrong Naples. Users are advised to be cautious as AI assistants may sometimes confirm bookings that are still pending.
